quote: the consul Caius Claudius nominated as dictator his colleague Marcus Livius
notes: Marcus Livius was named dictator to hold the consular elections, appointing Quintus Caecilius master of the horse (quote at livy:en:28:10).

quote: to make inquiry what states of the Tuscans and Umbrians had formed schemes of revolt from the Romans
notes: The dictator was sent by senate decree to Etruria to investigate which states had plotted revolt to Hasdrubal during his invasion (quote at livy:en:28:10).

quote: the vestal, who had the guarding of it for that night, was scourged by the command of Publius Licinius the pontiff
notes: Amid a wave of prodigies the fire of Vesta went out and the negligent vestal was scourged by the pontiff, with expiatory victims and a supplication decreed (quote at livy:en:28:11).

quote: issued an edict that all who were citizens of Cremona and Placentia should return to those colonies before a certain day
notes: After ambassadors of Placentia and Cremona complained of Gallic raids and depopulation, the consuls by senate decree ordered the colonists back — colony restoration rather than a new foundation (quote at livy:en:28:11).

quote: Besides, a mutiny arose in the camp at Sucro. Here were eight thousand men, stationed as a guard
notes: During the rumour of Scipio's death eight thousand troops at Sucro mutinied over arrears of pay, expelled their tribunes and conferred command and fasces on the privates Albius and Atrius (quote at livy:en:28:24).

quote: called together their countrymen the Lacetani, and summoning the Celtiberian youth to arms, devastated in a hostile manner the territories of the Suessetanians and Sedetanians, allies of the Romans
notes: Mandonius and Indibilis, disappointed of ruling Spain, rose against Rome's allies on the rumour of Scipio's death, then abandoned the attempt when he proved alive (quote at livy:en:28:24; lapse at 28:25).

quote: sending collectors round to the tributary states, to give the soldiers hopes of soon receiving their pay
notes: Seven military tribunes soothed the mutineers' pay grievances while Scipio raised money from tributary states and summoned the army to Carthage for payment (quote at livy:en:28:25).

quote: a warm debate took place as to whether they should visit with punishment the originators only of the mutiny
notes: Scipio's council debated and condemned the thirty-five ringleaders only, who were then lured to lodgings, plied with wine and arrested by stratagem (quote at livy:en:28:26).

quote: They were tied to the stake, scourged with rods, and decapitated
notes: After Scipio's reconciliation speech the condemned ringleaders were executed before the terrified assembly, which then re-took the oath of allegiance and received its pay (quote at livy:en:28:29).

quote: they again summoned their countrymen to arms; and assembling the auxiliaries which had joined them before
notes: Hearing of the severity shown the mutineers, Mandonius and Indibilis feared like punishment and rose again with 20,000 foot, until crushed in battle and pardoned (quote at livy:en:28:31; defeat and settlement 28:33-34).

quote: Scipio having without difficulty regained the affection of his soldiers, both by his punctuality in discharging the arrears of pay to all
notes: Scipio closed the Sucro affair by paying arrears to guilty and innocent alike and in an assembly redirected the army against the Ilergetian rebels (quote at livy:en:28:32).

quote: falling prostrate before his knees, ascribed his conduct to the fatal frenzy of those times
notes: After defeat Mandonius appealed to Scipio's clemency; Scipio spared the rebels, left them their arms and hostages untouched, and imposed only a fine to pay the troops (quote at livy:en:28:34).

quote: all the centuries, with the strongest marks of attachment, named Publius Scipio as consul
notes: After the senate declined his claim to a triumph, Scipio was elected consul by every century amid record crowds already dooming Africa to him as his province (quote at livy:en:28:38).

quote: It being generally reported that Africa, as a new province, was destined for Publius Scipio without casting lots
notes: Fabius opened the great senate debate against assigning Scipio the African command, charging personal ambition over the public good; Scipio replied at 28:43-44 (quote at livy:en:28:40).

quote: I require of you, tribunes of the people, to support me in refusing to give my opinion
notes: Fulvius invoked the tribunes against Scipio's threatened appeal to the people; their ruling forced the question into the senate, which gave Scipio Sicily with leave to cross to Africa (quote at livy:en:28:45).

quote: Scipio, though he could not obtain leave to levy troops, a point which he did not urge with great eagerness
notes: The senate denied Scipio a regular levy for the African expedition but allowed volunteers and voluntary allied contributions for building his fleet (quote at livy:en:28:45).

quote: the quaestors were ordered to sell a district of the Campanian territory extending from the Grecian trench to the sea
notes: For want of war funds the quaestors sold confiscated Campanian public land with informer rewards, while the city praetor policed where Campanians were permitted to dwell (quote at livy:en:28:46).
